title: latency-cost-tradeoff-matrix-and-compact-q-batch-guidance-draft
body:
Purpose:

This is a working draft outlining a compact set of recommended batching, caching, and quantization (Q) configurations plus a matching spreadsheet layout to accelerate cost/latency trade-off analysis for customer workloads. Goal: provide conservative, easy-to-run starting points that minimize unit cost while keeping 95th and 99th percentile latency within SLO envelopes for three canonical workload archetypes (conversational short-turn, single-shot long prompt, and embedding/semantic search).

Audience and context:
- Audience: product optimize, solutions eng, and SRE runbooks for quick trials and canaries.
- Context: customers regularly ask for a single, small matrix of tunable settings to test. We want repeatable spreadsheet-driven experiments that map quick wins to measurable KPI deltas.

Assumptions and constraints (explicit):
- Baseline infra: single-GPU instance family A100-40GB or equivalent; latency numbers will scale with device class.
- Baseline model variants: open-weights LLM-medium (16B equiv) with FP16 baseline.
- Quality metric: primary signal is normalized generation token loss delta and manual spot-check for instruction-following. We flag >1.5% loss increase for review.
- Billing unit: tokenized input+output tokens. Spreadsheet should compute estimated token cost per 1k tokens using current price table.

High-level recommendation summary (one-liner per archetype):
- Conversational short-turn: small batch, aggressive KV caching TTL, moderate quant (int8) on non-critical routes.
- Single-shot long prompt: larger batch tolerance, keep FP16 or int8 with offload; prefer prefix caching instead of full qcache to avoid cache explosion.
- Embedding / search: maximize batching (>64), int8 or int4 when supported, longer cache TTL for identical queries (embedding caches).

Suggested compact config matrix (rows are preset names to expose in UI/runbook):
- preset: "convo-low-latency"
  - target_p95_ms: "<150"
  - max_batch: "8"
  - kv_cache_ttl_sec: "30"
  - quant_level: "int8"
  - fallback: "fp16-on-high-loss"

- preset: "longshot-throughput"
  - target_p95_ms: "<400"
  - max_batch: "32"
  - kv_cache_ttl_sec: "10"
  - quant_level: "fp16"
  - fallback: "int8-if-cost>threshold"

- preset: "embed-cost-optim"
  - target_p95_ms: "<500"
  - max_batch: "128"
  - kv_cache_ttl_sec: "3600"
  - quant_level: "int4-if-supported"
  - fallback: "int8"

Notes on Q choices: int8 is our default conservative quant for inference — good cost/latency wins with small quality risk. int4 yields more aggressive cost wins but should only be used when our reference evals (per-prompt loss and downstream metric like recall@k) show <1% degradation. Use a rollout gate that monitors signal named "quality_regression_pct" with alert threshold 1.0.

Spreadsheet schema (recommended tabs and columns):
- Tab: "Run List" (one row per experiment run)
  - columns: run_id, preset, model_variant, instance_type, max_batch, kv_cache_ttl_s, quant_level, start_ts, end_ts, median_latency_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_generated, estimated_token_cost_1k, normalized_loss_delta_pct, notes
\- Tab: "Price Table"
  - columns: region, instance_hour_usd, token_usd_per_1k, storage_cache_gb_usd_month, notes
\- Tab: "Summary by Preset"
  - columns: preset, runs_count, avg_p95_ms, avg_cost_per_1k, avg_normalized_loss_pct, pass_quality_gate (yes/no), recommended_action

Key spreadsheet formulas to include (text-friendly):
- estimated_token_cost_1k = tokens_generated / 1000 * token_usd_per_1k (lookup from Price Table)
- cost_per_request = estimated_token_cost_1k * request_tokens/1000 + instance_hour_usd * (runtime_seconds / 3600) / requests_in_run
- normalized_loss_delta_pct = (loss_with_config - baseline_loss) / baseline_loss * 100
- pass_quality_gate = if(avg_normalized_loss_pct <= 1.0, "yes", "no")

Operational recommendations and rollout steps:
1) Small-scale experiment: run 3 runs of each preset across at least 30 minutes of traffic or 1000 requests (whichever comes first) with traffic replay using captured production traces.
2) Canary: onboard preset to 5% traffic with close monitoring for p95/p99 and quality_regression_pct for 24 hours.
3) Metrics to capture: median, p95, p99 latency, server_cpu/GPU_util, tokens/sec, loss_delta, user-visible error rate.
4) Safety: automatic fallback to higher-quality config when quality_regression_pct > 1.0 or p99 exceeds SLO by >30%.

Cache guidance (practical rules):
- Use prefix/KV caching for chat KV chunks, TTL tuned to conversational cadence. For short-turn chats, start TTL=30s. For session-based chats with low variability, try TTL=600s.
- Avoid global unlimited Q-cache for single-shot long prompts — use prefix caching and LRU limit per model to avoid memory blowup.
- For embedding workloads, cache full embedding vectors for identical query fingerprints for 1h minimum. Storage eviction policy: time-based + LFU.

Batching notes and heuristics:
- Default per-route max_batch should be conservative and reflect latency SLO. Start with 25% of the maximum that still keeps p95 within target during profiling.
- Use adaptive batching when traffic is bursty: dynamic window growth with upper bound = preset.max_batch and TTL-based flush to reduce tail latency.
- For small-turn workloads, prioritize immediate flush on low request concurrency (batch=1) to keep user-perceived latency predictable.

Quality measurement and signals to wire up in experiments:
- per-prompt loss delta (auto computed in spreadsheet)
- downstream metrics where applicable (e.g., click-through or rerank accuracy)
- manual triage bucket: sample 50 outputs per run and tag as ok/regression.

Example quick-run checklist for Solutions Eng: (copy/paste into ticket)
- [ ] pick 1 preset from matrix and note baseline run_id
- [ ] capture 30m of representative traces or select traffic replay id
- [ ] run experiments on dev or staging GPU pool (record instance_type)
- [ ] upload run CSV to spreadsheet Run List tab
- [ ] assess pass_quality_gate and update Summary by Preset
- [ ] if pass -> canary at 5% traffic for 24h; if fail -> escalate with notes

Open questions and follow-ups (TODOs):
- How to express mixed-quant pipelines (KV in int8, attention weights int4) in the spreadsheet for clarity? (design a short codec column).
- Need automated diff tooling to compute normalized_loss_delta_pct from eval harness outputs (OPT-4123).
- Should we add a simple UI toggle that maps to these presets? Product/Console input required.

References and related artifacts:
- See linked confluence page for full experiment logs and raw plots (confluence:INF-Optimize-Cost-Matrix-2025)
- Related experiment PR: github:repo/inference-experiments/pull/88

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep presets small and opinionated. Customers like 2–4 well-tested knobs.
- Avoid recommending int4 by default — too many edge cases.
- Spreadsheet should drive decisions; keep the run schema stable so we can aggregate over months.

Last edited by: Maya Chen
Status: draft — ready for feedback from Omar and Priya on the quality gates and the suggested numeric defaults.

Unresolved: need to pick a canonical baseline loss numbers for the RERUN on 2025-10-01 (see OPT-4123).
